summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: The package ships a `postinstall` hook that executes `beacon.cjs`, and its `main` entry (`index.js`) top-level requires and invokes the same beacon, so both `npm install` and any `require('@kibt/www-nuxt-i18n')` cause an HTTP POST to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`. The payload contains `os.hostname()`, the package install path (`__dirname`), `process.cwd()`, and a `npm/<node version>` user-agent string. The destination is a bare IPv4 host over plain HTTP, not a publisher domain, and has no TLS. The package exports only an inert Proxy that returns no-op functions for every property access and self-describes as a 'Compatibility shim' / 'Build-provenance beacon', so it ships no functionality beyond the phone-home — the shape of a dependency-confusion / typosquat reconnaissance package where the beacon maps internal consumers of the `@kibt` scope to attacker infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
